chunks: And ʿUthmān ibn Ziyād narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: We had a camel driver working for us, and he loaded it onto someone else, so it was lost.
He said: Make him liable and take compensation from him.

key_terms.جَمَّالًا: a camel driver or transporter hired to carry goods
key_terms.ضَمِّنْهُ: hold him legally liable for compensation
key_terms.عَلَى غَيْرِهِ: onto someone other than himself or his own conveyance
key_terms.فَحَمَلَ: he transported or loaded the goods
key_terms.يُكَارِينَا: he used to hire out his carrying service to us

ai.seo_question: Is a hired carrier liable if he transfers goods to someone else and they are lost?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on liability when an entrusted carrier transfers a load to another party and the property is then lost. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the original carrier is financially responsible, establishing accountability in entrusted commercial dealings.
